chunks: Jābir narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:

The first matter concerning which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will judge on the Day of qiyamah is bloodshed. Then the two sons of Adam عليه السلام will be made to stand, and judgment will be made between them; then those after them among the people of bloodshed, until none of them remains from among the people. After that, the slain one will come with his killer, and his blood will gush upon his face, and he will say: You killed him; so he will not be able to conceal any statement from Allah.

key_terms.ابْنَا آدَمَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: the two sons of Adam عليه السلام, presented as the first case of bloodshed
key_terms.الدِّمَاءُ: bloodshed; unlawful killing and the spilling of blood
key_terms.الْمَقْتُولُ: the slain person who seeks justice
key_terms.بِقَاتِلِهِ: with his killer; the murderer brought for judgment
key_terms.فَيَشْخُبَ دَمُهُ: his blood gushes forth, vividly indicating the claim against the killer
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment, when final reckoning takes place

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about bloodshed being judged first on the Day of qiyamah?
ai.summary: This hadith states that bloodshed is the first matter judged by Allah on the Day of qiyamah, emphasizing the gravity of unlawfully taking life. It portrays a scene of ultimate accountability in which the slain confront their killers directly, and no one is able to hide the truth before Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5166 - Jabir narrated from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"The first matter that Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, will judge on the Day of Judgment is bloodshed.
The sons of Adam (as) will be brought forward, and judgment will be passed between them.
Then those who followed them among the people of bloodshed will be judged until none of them remain.
After that, the murdered will bring forth his killer, and his blood will gush onto the killer's face.
The murdered will say: 'You killed me,' and the killer will not be able to conceal any word from Allah (swt)."
